On minors of non-hamiltonian graphs



On-Hei Solomon Lo

Abstract
    

A theorem of Tutte states that every 4-connected non-hamiltonian graph contains K3,3K_{3,3} as a minor. We strengthen this result by proving that such a graph must contain K3,4K_{3,4} as a minor, thereby confirming a special case of a conjecture posed by Chen, Yu, and Zang in a strong form.

1 Introduction




In 1956, Tutte [18] proved that every 4-connected planar graph is hamiltonian. This groundbreaking theorem has inspired a wealth of subsequent research. Notably, Thomas and Yu [17] extended it to projective-planar graphs. However, a longstanding conjecture, proposed independently by Grünbaum [6] and Nash-Williams [14], remains largely unresolved: Every 4-connected toroidal graph is hamiltonian. For further developments on extensions to graphs embedded in surfaces, we refer the reader to [15]. In this paper, we consider Tutte’s theorem from a different perspective.




A classical theorem due to Hall [7] and Wagner [20] establishes that every 3-connected non-planar graph is either isomorphic to K5K_{5} or contains a K3,3K_{3,3} minor. Consequently, Tutte’s theorem is equivalent to asserting that every 4-connected non-hamiltonian graph contains a K3,3K_{3,3} minor. Another well-known result of Wagner [19] shows that every 4-connected non-planar graph contains a K5K_{5} minor. Together with Tutte’s theorem, this implies that every 4-connected non-hamiltonian graph also contains a K5K_{5} minor. These results motivate our investigation of minors in non-hamiltonian graphs.

Characterizing minor-minimal 4-connected non-hamiltonian graphs enhances the aforementioned results, as it allows one to verify that every such graph contains both a K3,3K_{3,3} minor and a K5K_{5} minor. In pursuit of this, we answer the following question posed by Ding and Marshall [5] affirmatively, thereby improving the theorem of Tutte.



Question 1.1 (Ding and Marshall [5]).



Does every 44-connected non-hamiltonian graph contain a minor of K3,4K_{3,4}?





It is worth noting that the connectivity requirement in Tutte’s theorem cannot be relaxed: there exist 3-connected non-hamiltonian graphs that do not contain a K3,3K_{3,3} minor. Despite this, Chen and Yu [2] proved that every 3-connected graph GG with no K3,3K_{3,3} minor contains a cycle of length at least α⋅|V⁡(G)|log3⁡2\alpha\cdot|V(G)|^{\log_{3}2} for some constant α>0\alpha>0. Moreover, the exponent log3⁡2\log_{3}2 is known to be optimal. This result was later extended by Chen, Yu, and Zang [3], who showed that for every integer t>3t>3, any 3-connected graph GG with no K3,tK_{3,t} minor contains a cycle of length at least α⁡(t)⋅|V⁡(G)|β\alpha(t)\cdot|V(G)|^{\beta}, where α⁡(t)=(1/2)t⁡(t−1)\alpha(t)=(1/2)^{t(t-1)} and β=log1729⁡2\beta=\log_{1729}2. They further conjectured that a linear bound should hold in the 4-connected case.



Conjecture 1.2 (Chen, Yu, and Zang [3]).



For each integer t≥4t\geq 4, there exists a function α⁡(t)>0\alpha(t)>0 such that every 4-connected graph GG with no K3,tK_{3,t} minor contains a cycle of length at least α⁡(t)⋅|V⁡(G)|\alpha(t)\cdot|V(G)|.





Our solution to Question 1.1 confirms Chen, Yu, and Zang’s conjecture for the case t=4t=4, with α⁡(4)=1\alpha(4)=1.
